doc.title: Bob Rosengarden interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 6, 1996

title: Hamilton visits and last night's concert with Clark Terry
summary: Rosengarden praises the previous night's concert and Clark Terry's knack for getting players going with minimal rehearsal.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: We are here today on behalf of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive with drummer/ percussionist Bob Rosengarden, a friend of Hamilton, and you’ve made how many annual trips here?
Many, many, many, thanks to Milt Fillius.
It’s a pleasure to have you again, and last night’s concert was—

You know I’m not being false modesty and any of that kind of stuff. It was one of the better ones. Clark is, Clark Terry has the knack, he’s a catalyst and he makes everybody — he kicks everybody in the butt and makes them play, whether they want to or not.
The people watching this didn’t get the benefit to see the rehearsal that went into that, but — the five minutes.
In five minutes at dinner he says here’s what we’re going to do, and if it’s okay with everybody. And it’s an education to watch that.

Well we’ve all known each other for so long. I mean you know your business, and I know my business. And we know there’s a lot of things you don’t have to say. Because if you have to say them it’s too late.
